Finally, X touches A, C, and D, and they are respectively blue, green, and orange, therefore X can only be red.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Each area in the picture on the right should be coloured using one of the colours red (R), green (G), blue (B) or orange (O). Areas which touch must be different colours. Which colour is the area marked X?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Each area in the picture on the right should be coloured using one of the colours red (R), green (G), blue (B) or orange (O). Areas which touch must be different colours. Which colour is the area marked X?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a spiral-shaped partition diagram. In the center there are three regions with colors already marked: R is above, G is below, and O is to their right. Around the center there are also several layers of unmarked regions: immediately outside R, G, and O is one large region; below it there is another horizontal region; between O and the far-right X there is a vertical region; at the bottom left there is a horizontal region; the entire far-right region is marked as X.

Reasoning: Let the inner unmarked region immediately next to R, G, and O be A. Because A touches R, G, and O respectively, A cannot be red, green, or orange, and can only be blue. Let the unmarked region below G/O be B. B touches G, O, and A, so B cannot be green, orange, or blue, and can only be red. Let the vertical unmarked region to the left of X and to the right of O/B be C. C touches O, A, and B, so C cannot be orange, blue, or red, and can only be green. Let the horizontal strip at the lower left be D. D touches A, B, and C, so D cannot be blue, red, or green, and can only be orange. Finally, X touches A, C, and D, and they are respectively blue, green, and orange, therefore X can only be red.
